---
title: "Analysis"
---


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggokabeito)   # color-blind-safe (Okabe-Ito) scale
data(penguins)
penguins <- penguins |> filter(!is.na(bill_len), !is.na(bill_dep), !is.na(body_mass))
```
:::


## Body mass by species


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(penguins, aes(species, body_mass, fill = species)) +
  geom_boxplot(show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_okabe_ito() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Body mass (g)")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Body mass by species.](analysis_files/figure-html/fig-mass-1.png){#fig-mass fig-alt='Boxplot of penguin body mass in grams by species. Gentoo is the heaviest, Adelie and Chinstrap overlap.' width=672}
:::
:::


@fig-mass shows that Gentoo penguins are clearly the heaviest of the three species.

## Mean measurements


::: {#tbl-means .cell tbl-cap='Mean measurements by species.'}

```{.r .cell-code}
penguins |>
  summarise(
    bill_len = mean(bill_len),
    bill_dep = mean(bill_dep),
    body_mass = mean(body_mass),
    .by = species
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


|species   | bill_len| bill_dep| body_mass|
|:---------|--------:|--------:|---------:|
|Adelie    |     38.8|     18.3|    3700.7|
|Gentoo    |     47.5|     15.0|    5076.0|
|Chinstrap |     48.8|     18.4|    3733.1|
